issues.concern: The English translation uses 'I stuff' which implies a continuous or habitual action, but the Japanese '入れる' (ireru) in this context is more likely a single, completed action or a general statement of purpose.
issues.suggestion: Change 'I stuff cotton into the plush toy.' to 'Stuff cotton into the plush toy.' (imperative, general instruction) or 'To stuff cotton into a plush toy.' (infinitive, general purpose) or 'I will stuff cotton into the plush toy.' (future action).
